title: Let's take a look at Escape from Stalingrad Z!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QLdp2ZNFM_s

Daniel (@dungeondive) shares first impressions, not a final review, of Escape from Stalingrad Z, a weird-WWII narrative skirmish game in which German and Soviet soldiers stranded in the corpse city of 1942 team up against the dead. He loves the format. The core box holds a ring-bound scenario and map book with roughly fifty branching missions, standees and dual-layer boards, and there's an even slimmer file-folder edition with everything needed to play.

The maps never grow beyond a two-page spread, and that's the point: it feels like a claustrophobic zombie film, or Space Hulk. Movement is brutally tight. You get four points, turning costs a point, and stepping diagonally or backwards costs two. Attacks are rolled one die at a time, because stunning a zombie first sets up a teammate's kill. Zombie types run from the basic beta through the exploding toxic ones to alphas that move twice and strengthen everything around them. Your campaign starts with one soldier and recruits up to four, and benched soldiers help hold spawns off the map. Lose the crew or exhaust your retries and the campaign is over.

He admits tactical games aren't his strength and he found it stressful. The characters are blank slates that only start to differ around 35 and 90 XP, several early missions can't be played co-op, and the rulebook has gaps, though a designer video and errata help. At around $50 he still recommends it, and he'd love a fantasy dungeon-crawl version in the same box.

----

Escape from Stalingrad Z makes every square of movement a decision. Do you enjoy tight tactical puzzles like this, or prefer skirmish games where you can just charge in?
